alignments.note: The negative indefinite is rendered discontinuously as 'not ... anything' (rule 15); head on the indefinite word, as rule 69 heads such a unit on 'any'.
Finite verb with its subject pronoun.
The substantival article's pronoun has already been written by οὐδέν as 'anything', so nothing is left for it and the participle keeps the relativizer and copula (rule 32).
Participle rendered as a finite relative clause with its supplied copula.
Nominalizing article of the articular infinitive (rule 61).
Pleonastic negative in the complement of a verb of shrinking; English does not double the negation, so no word answers to it (rule 79's reasoning).
The English 'from ...-ing' is the marker of this infinitival complement and is its own helper (rule 61).
Dative pronoun with the English preposition realizing its case (rule 21).
Infinitive rendered by the English gerund.
Distributive κατά rendered by the discontinuous frame 'from ... to' (rule 15); the noun keeps its two occurrences.
The noun's two English occurrences form one unit; joining all four words into a single unit would fail rule 94's count test.

review_notes: οὐδέν takes the whole discontinuous 'not ... anything' and the pleonastic μή is left unrepresented; the alternative of giving 'not' to μή is defensible but would leave the indefinite carrying no negation while a plain negator stands empty.
κατ᾽ οἴκους is split into 'from ... to' and 'house ... house' rather than made one unit, following rule 94.
